Definition: from a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed σελγής (of uncertain derivation, but apparently meaning continent); licentiousness (sometimes including other vices):--filthy, lasciviousness, wantonness.
BiblicalUsage: Lasciviousness is wantonness without shame, the flesh let loose, and the apostles name it in their lists of sins. It is a work of the flesh in Galatians, the Gentiles give themselves over to it to work all uncleanness with greediness, Peter says the time past of our life may suffice to have wrought it, and Lot is delivered, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe lasciviousness is the sin of a conscience gone numb: not a fall in a weak moment, but a life given over to uncleanness with greediness. Lot is the proof that a righteous soul can live in the middle of it and be vexed day by day, and I hold that the gospel's answer is not better management but a new heart that wants to be clean.
